report:
Reviewed the complete parse.dependencies claim, all nine implementation associations and sole TODO test; captured the modules design. Source inspection only; no test execution or source changes.

The claim permits source, scope, edition, compilation configuration and generated parse inputs, while forbidding resolved names, checked interfaces, other checked bodies and trait results. mods.rs unexpanded_items is the tracked module parse boundary: file-backed modules pass SourceFile text and module scope into parse_str_to_cst; inline modules receive their syntactic item list through specification rather than calling semantic checking. parse/mod.rs constructs a parser from explicit text/source/scope and walks syntax. attrs.rs consults compilation cfg values before item identity construction and otherwise parses attribute syntax. exprs.rs, generics.rs, paths.rs and types.rs build CST nodes and intern textual names rather than resolving them or invoking type/trait checking. util.rs computes text/name/span information from the parse node and source. items.rs constructs item identities/CST, records lexical scopes and edition, and assigns inline child items to their own modules.

The file-resolution helpers named resolve_mod_file/module_directory are source-path discovery from file path and enclosing module scope, not semantic name resolution. They inspect source-file availability for implicit or explicit module paths; no callee body or checked interface is requested. Parsing function body syntax into CST is likewise not checking another item's body. Generated ParseSource is carried for provenance; this parser entry receives its text rather than asking the trait solver to derive it. Searches and inspection of the associated parser files found no semantic resolve/prove/signature/body query in this path. This is a source-level dependency assessment, not a measured cold/warm query trace.

The only associated evidence entry modules_parse_dependencies is TODO and has no assertions. It requires a cold parse input whitelist, zero parse work on unchanged warm requests, and reuse after semantic-only changes. Completing that trace and persistent-edit matrix across ordinary/generated parsing and configuration/scope inputs is the prerequisite for full verification. I preserve this deferral rather than treating the absence of obvious forbidden calls or the implementation markers as exhaustive transitive/runtime proof. All nine entries and permitted/forbidden dependency categories are accounted for, no concrete additional defect was identified and no edits are requested.
